chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Sa'd ibn Sa'd, from Safwan, from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:
If you do not know how many (rak'at) you have prayed and your doubt does not settle on a specific number, then repeat the prayer.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one doubts the number of rak'at prayed but has no specific doubt?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Kafi addresses the principle of 'general doubt' (shakk al-mutlaq) where the worshipper lacks a specific inclination (wahm) toward a particular number of rak'at. Unlike cases where a specific doubt triggers the 'building on certainty' (ibna' ala al-mahkum bihi) rule, this scenario requires rebuilding the prayer from scratch to ensure validity, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on caution in acts of worship. This distinction highlights the nuanced methodology of Usuli scholars in differentiating between mere uncertainty and decisive doubt.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Sa’ad Bin Sa’ad, from Safwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If it was so that you did not know how many (Rak’at) you have prayed and your imagination does not fall upon anything, so repeat the Salāt’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Sa‘d ibn Sa‘d from Safwan who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If you do not know how many Rak‘at you have performed and your guess does not settle anywhere, perform your Salah (prayer) again.’”
